_readme: This file defines, per instruction FORMAT (see the 'format' column of
aurora_v1_2_isa.json), the exact bit position of every sub-field of the
16-bit instruction word, so a mnemonic + operands can be packed into a
literal integer (and unpacked back).
Every field bit-range is inclusive [hi, lo], matching the datasheet's own
'15:12' style notation.
'status' is either:
normative - the exact field layout is stated (as a bit diagram or a
fully-worked binary/hex example) in AUR-ARCH-005 and its
addenda (extracted from the .docx sources under docs/).
inferred  - AUR-ARCH-005 itself says the sub-byte field layout for this
format is NOT YET RATIFIED ('Fields below bit 8 are
format-dependent; instruction-specific pages must state
their exact interpretation' / 'Future instruction-family
revisions will add complete per-instruction operand-field
diagrams'). The layout below is a reasonable, internally
consistent placeholder designed by extension of the
normative formats, ONLY so that mnemonic->bits translation
is possible today. Treat as provisional pending an ADR.
RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (was: KNOWN OPEN CONFLICT):
0xC0/0xC1 are locked as LOOP/NOP (format LOOP_IMM8) per ADR-ISA-020 and
ADR-FE-006. AGUCFG(0xC2)/STRIDE(0xC3) - never backed by any ADR - are
RETIRED per ADR-ISA-022 and removed from the DB. 0xC2 is reallocated
to LOOPR (format LOOP_REG, register-supplied loop count), also per
ADR-ISA-022. 0xC3-0xC9 remain reserved.
ALSO NEW 2026-08-04: POPMETA allocated a real opcode (0xB9, format
STREAM_POPMETA) per ADR-STREAM-009, closing the 'reserved, not
allocated' gap left by ADR-STREAM-008. MAC/MAS operand 0 corrected
from a bare GPR placeholder to an explicit accumulator selector per
ADR-DSP-018. Every instruction gained operand_spec_confidence/
encoding_spec_confidence/semantic_spec_confidence/sources/notes
fields (see isa/database/apply_proposal_fix_issues_1.py).

RRR.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3/5 (worked example ADD R1,R1,R2 = 0x0012)

RRR_OR_ACC.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.5 (worked example DIVSTEP R1,R1,R2 = 0x3412); MUL/MULH/DIVSTEP/DIV share the same physical layout and 2-address (Rd=Ra) convention
RRR_OR_ACC.note: subop only ever takes values 0-5 (MUL/MULH/MAC/MAS/DIVSTEP/DIV) so 3 bits (10:8) fully cover it; bit 11 is unused/reserved (must be 0) for this format's own mnemonics (MUL/MULH/DIVSTEP/DIV). MAC/MAS repurpose that freed bit 11 as an accumulator selector - see format RRR_ACC, ADR-DSP-018.

RRR_ACC.note: MAC/MAS physically share primary=0x3 and the subop numbering (2=MAC, 3=MAS) with RRR_OR_ACC's other members, but unlike those 2-address (Rd=Ra) ops, Ra/Rb here are two genuinely independent register operands: bit 11 (always 0/unused across RRR_OR_ACC's subop range 0-5) is a dedicated acc_sel bit (0=A0, 1=A1) rather than part of a 2-address destination field.

RRI.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3 Operand Format Diagrams

extension.mechanism: attach one 0xE EXT word immediately after; EXT word supplies the additional high-order immediate bits (merge rule: EXT low 12 bits are the sign-extended upper bits, concatenated above IMM4)

SHIFT.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3 Operand Format Diagrams

MEM.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3 Operand Format Diagrams

extension.mechanism: attach one 0xE EXT word supplying the extra displacement bits

BR.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3 Operand Format Diagrams; Sec.4 B.* inventory (0x80-0x87)

extension.trigger: branch target out of +/-128 byte-pair range of disp8
extension.mechanism: attach one 0xE EXT word supplying extended displacement

CTRL.source: AUR-ARCH-005 only lists CALL/JMP/RET/JMPR at the mnemonic+opcode level (Sec.4, 0x90-0x93); no sub-byte field diagram is published
CTRL.note: JMPR reads bits [3:0] as Rs (register-indirect target), remaining bits reserved=0. CALL/JMP read bits [7:0] as a signed PC-relative displacement (extendable via 0xE EXT word, same mechanism as BR). RET takes no operand (field ignored, must be 0).

STACK.source: AUR-ARCH-005 only lists PUSH/POP/PUSHM/POPM at the mnemonic+opcode level (Sec.4, 0xA0-0xA3); no sub-byte field diagram is published
STACK.note: PUSH/POP (single-register form) use bits [7:4] as Rs/Rd; PAIRED64 mode pushes/pops an aligned register pair named by the same field. PUSHM/POPM (multi-register form) cannot fit a 16-entry register mask in the remaining byte: they MUST attach one 0xE EXT word whose low 16 bits are the full register mask (bit i => Ri included), with the base word's [7:4] field unused/reserved=0.

STREAM.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3 combined STREAM/SYSTEM Operand Format Diagram
STREAM.note: select picks Q0 vs Q1 (bit 6) plus one spare mode bit (bit 7); control_arg carries a register number, small immediate, or sub-field selector depending on the instruction. QCFG additionally decodes control_arg per the QCFG_FIELD table below.

STREAM_QSTEP.source: AUR-ARCH-005 'Pinned Circular Streams v1.2h' addendum, explicit bit diagram: 15:12=1011, 11:8=1000, 7:4=Qn/0, 3:0=reserved(0)

QCFG_FIELD.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2c/h addenda define the QCFG field enumeration (ADDR, INNER_STRIDE, INNER_COUNT, OUTER_ADJUST, OUTER_COUNT, WIDTH, END_MODE) and syntax 'QCFG Qn, field, Rs/imm' but not a sub-byte bit diagram

extension.trigger: always for register/immediate value operand (no room left in base word)
extension.mechanism: attach one 0xE EXT word whose low bits carry Rs (register form) or the immediate value

SYSTEM.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2d Sec.3 combined STREAM/SYSTEM Operand Format Diagram (shared layout)
SYSTEM.note: Used by MRS/MSR/EI/DI/IRET/ASCALL/TIMERLOAD/TIMERVEC/TIMERCTL/RDCYCLE. control_arg carries the system-register selector or small immediate.

SYSTEM_NONE.source: AUR-ARCH-005 'System Architecture Update v1.2e' addendum: generic encoding diagram 15:12=1101 / 11:8=subop(B-F) / instruction-specific bits, with WFI/WFE/HALT stated to take no operand

SYSTEM_CTX.source: AUR-ARCH-005 v1.2e addendum defines the 8-bit Context Mask Groups table (bits 0-7 = VOLATILE_GPR..FULL) for CTXSAVE/CTXRESTORE 'Rbase, mask' operands, but the mask table alone fully occupies the remaining byte, leaving no room for Rbase in the base word

extension.trigger: always (Rbase has no room in the base word)
extension.mechanism: mandatory attached 0xE EXT word; bits [3:0] of the EXT word supply Rbase

MODE_IMM.source: AUR-ARCH-005 'Revision 1.2c: MODE and Two-Dimensional Streams' addendum, explicit bit diagram: 15:12=1101, 11:8=1010, 7:5=mode, 4:0=reserved(0)

RR_OR_UNARY.source: AUR-ARCH-005 lists PACK/UNPACK/ZIP/UNZIP/BSWAP/WSWAP/SHUFFLE/MOV at the mnemonic+opcode level only, but the 'Extension and Bounds Faults v1.2f' addendum gives a normative worked layout for the same family's ZEXT8/SEXT8/ZEXT16/SEXT16 (Rd, Rs two-register form) which is reused here for consistency
RR_OR_UNARY.note: For strictly-unary ops (BSWAP, WSWAP) bits [3:0] are reserved=0. SHUFFLE's lane-select immediate reuses bits [3:0] in place of Rb.

DSP_RED.source: AUR-ARCH-005 lists REDUCE.* at the mnemonic+opcode level only (Sec.4, 0x40/0x41); no sub-byte field diagram is published

DSP_DOT.source: AUR-ARCH-005 lists DOT at the mnemonic+opcode level only (Sec.4, 0x48); needs two source operands, which do not fit in the 8 bits remaining after subop

extension.trigger: always (second source register has no room in the base word)
extension.mechanism: mandatory attached 0xE EXT word; bits [3:0] supply src1

DSP_SAD.source: AUR-ARCH-005 lists SAD at the mnemonic+opcode level only (Sec.4, 0x49); same two-source constraint as DSP_DOT

extension.trigger: always (second source register has no room in the base word)
extension.mechanism: mandatory attached 0xE EXT word; bits [3:0] supply src1

LOOP_REG.source: ADR-ISA-022 (locked 2026-08-04): register-count sibling to LOOP_IMM8, allocated at the opcode AGUCFG/STRIDE vacated. No prior docx bit diagram existed; this ADR is the normative definition.
LOOP_REG.note: Iteration count is read from Rs at LOOPR retirement (unsigned, must be nonzero - a zero count is illegal). Same NOP-terminated body machinery, restrictions, and eight-word capture window as LOOP_IMM8/ADR-ISA-020/ADR-FE-006.

LOOP_IMM8.source: AUR-ARCH-005 'Hardware Loop Update v1.2g' addendum, explicit bit diagram: 15:12=1100, 11:8=0000(LOOP)/0001(NOP), 7:0=count_minus_one (LOOP only). Adopted 2026-08-04 per ADR-ISA-020 (locked) / ADR-FE-006 (locked); isa/database/aurora_v1_2_isa.json updated (LOOPSET->LOOP, LOOPEND->NOP).
LOOP_IMM8.note: Iterations = count_minus_one + 1 (range 1-256). NOP (subop=1) ignores bits [7:0], must be 0.

STREAM_POPMETA.source: ADR-STREAM-009 (locked 2026-08-04, amended 2026-08-04): fresh opcode allocation for the POPMETA concept ADR-STREAM-008 left 'reserved, not allocated'. Amendment removed the ORD/ADDR meta selector; POPMETA always returns address.
STREAM_POPMETA.note: Rd receives the popped value; the adjacent register Rd+1 (not separately encoded, same convention as other aligned-pair forms) always receives the popped element's address (Qn.ADDR_LAST). The former ORD_LAST option and its selector bit were retired 2026-08-04 along with the Qn.ORD_NEXT/ORD_LAST system registers.

EXT.source: AUR-ARCH-005 Sec.6 Encoding Rules: '0xE extension words belong to the preceding base instruction and cannot be branch targets.' No merge-rule bit diagram is published for how EXT payload combines with each base format.
EXT.note: Merge rule with the preceding base word is instruction/format specific (see each format's 'extension' entry above); no single universal rule is confirmed.

CUSTOM.source: AUR-ARCH-005 Sec.6 Encoding Rules: '0xF is reserved for implementation-defined/custom expansion and must trap when unsupported.'
